lines.text: Do you know how deleting a file works? When you delete a photo, it usually isn't gone. Not right away.
First it goes to a trash folder. On an iPhone, Recently Deleted keeps it for thirty days.
After that, your storage works like a library. An index keeps track of where every piece of every file is stored.
Deleting mostly just erases that index entry and marks the space as free. The data itself stays there, until something new is written over it.
That's why recovery tools can scan the raw storage and stitch old files back together.
Phones and newer laptops use flash memory, which clears freed blocks in the background. So recovery there is much harder.
And modern phones encrypt everything. A factory reset throws away the key, so the old data turns into noise.
But copies live on. Cloud backups, chat apps, and the servers your file passed through.
Orbi locks every file on your phone before it's sent. And by default, after 30 minutes, the locked pieces on the server are deleted for good.
